source_text: Qui vero non hic, id est, non intra hunc ambitum terrae, nec per hunc commeatum vitae, nec apud homines hujus naturae communis confessionem putant constitutam, quanta praesumptio est adversus omnem ordinem rerum in terris istis, et in vita ista, et sub humanis potestatibus experiundarum? Nimirum cum animae de corporibus excesserint, et per singula tabulata coelorum de praecepto dispici coeperint, et interrogari arcana illa haereticorum sacramenta, tunc confitendum apud veras potestates et veros homines, Theletos scilicet et Abascantos et Acinetos Valentini. Nostrates enim, inquiunt, nec ipse Demiurgus constanter homines probabat veros esse, quos stillicidium situlae et pulverem areae et sputamen et locustas deputavit; etiam irrationalibus jumentis adaequavit. Plane ita scriptum. Non tamen idcirco aliud hominis genus intelligendum praeter nos: quos quia constat esse, et comparatione potuit induere, salva et proprietate generis, et singularitate. Neque enim si vita vitiata est, ut despectui judicata despectis compararetur, statim natura sublata est, ut alia in nomine ejus deputaretur. Atquin servatur natura, etsi suffunditur vita, nec alios novit Christus homines, quam de quibus dicit: Quem me aiunt esse homines? et: Quomodo vultis ut faciant vobis homines, et ita vos facite illis. Vide an servaverit genus, a quibus et testimonium sui exspectet, et in quos justitiae vicem mandat. Illos autem coelestes homines si expostulem mihi ostendi, facilius Aratus Persea, et Cephea, et Erigonam, et Ariadnam inter sidera deliniabit. Quis autem prohibuit Dominum illic etiam confessionem hominum faciendam manifeste determinare, ubi suam futuram aperte pronuntiavit? ut ita esset positum: «Qui in me confessus fuerit coram hominibus in coelis, et ego in illo confitebor coram Patre meo qui in coelis est?» Eripere me debuit ex isto terrenae confessionis errore, quam suscipi noluit, si coelestem praecepisset, quia nullos alios homines noveram praeter incolas terrae; ne ipso quidem adhuc tunc in coelis homine conspecto. Quae porro fides rerum, ut post excessum ad superna sublevatus, illic probarer, quo non nisi jam probatus imponerer? illic de praecepto examinarer, quo nisi admittendus pervenire non possem? Christiano coelum ante patet quam via; quia nulla via in coelum, nisi cui patet coelum; quod qui attigerit, intrabit. Quas mihi potestates janitrices affirmas juxta romanam superstitionem Janum quemdam et Forculum et Limentinum? quas a cancellis ordinas potestates? Si unquam legisti apud David, auferte portas principes vestras, et subleventur portae aeternae, et intrabit rex gloriae. Si item audisti apud Amos: Qui assensum illum suum aedificat in coelos, et profusionem suam fundat in terras; scito et ascensum illum exinde complanatum vestigiis Domini, et introitum exinde reseratum viribus Christi, nec ullam moram aut quaestionem in limine Christianis occursuram, qui non dignosci habeant illic, sed agnosci; nec interrogari, sed admitti. Nam et si adhuc clausum putas coelum, memento claves ejus hic Dominum Petro, et per eum, Ecclesiae reliquisse, quas hic unusquisque interrogatus atque confessus feret secum. Sed asseverat diabolus illic confitendum, ut suadeat hic negandum. Pulchra videlicet documenta praemittam, bonas mecum claves feram, timorem eorum, qui solum corpus occidunt, animae autem nihil faciunt: commendatus ero hujus praecepti desertione; honeste in coelestibus stabo, qui in terrenis stare non potui; sustinebo majores potestates, qui minoribus cessi; merebor denique admitti, jam exclusus. Suppetit adhuc dicere: si in coelestibus confitendum, et hic negandum est; nam ubi alterum, ibi utrumque; aemula enim quaeque concurrunt. Etiam persecutionem in coelis agitari oportebit, quae confessionis negationisve materia est. Quid itaque cessas, audacissime haeretice, totum ordinem christianae concussionis in superna transferre, et in primis, ipsum nominis odium illic collocare, ubi ad Patris dexteram praesidet Christus? Illic constitues et synagogas Judaeorum, fontes persecutionum, apud quas Apostoli flagella perpessi sunt, et populos nationum cum suo quidem circo, ubi facile conclamant, «Usquequo genus tertium?» Sed et fratres nostros et patres et filios et socrus et nurus et domesticos nostros ibidem exhibere debebis, per quos traditio disposita est: item reges et praesides et armatas potestates, apud quos caussa purganda est. Erit certe etiam carcer in coelo, carens sole, aut ingratis luminosus, et vincula fortasse de zonis, et equuleus axis ipse qui torquet: tum si lapidandus christianus, grandines aderunt; si urendus, fulmina prae manu sunt; si trucidandus, Orionis armati manus operabitur; si bestiis finiendus, ursas septemtrio emittet, zodiacus tauros et leones. Haec qui sustinuerit in finem, iste erit salvus. Ergone et finis in coelis, et passio, et occisio, et prima confessio? Et ubi caro, omnibus istis necessaria? ubi corpus? quod solum ab hominibus habet occidi. Haec nobis etiam ludicrum in modum certa ratio mandavit, nec ullus obicem praescriptionis istius extrudet, ut non omnem ordinem persecutionis, omnem ejus caussae firmam paraturam illuc transferre cogatur, ubi confessioni forum dederit. Siquidem confessio a persecutione deducitur, et persecutio in confessione finitur. Nec possunt non una sequi, quae et aditum et exitum, id est, initium finemque disponunt. Porro et odium nominis hic erit, et persecutio hic erumpit, et traditio hic producit, et interrogatio hic compellit, et carnificina hic desaevit, et totum hunc ordinem in terris confessio vel negatio expungit. Igitur si caetera hic, nec confessio alibi; si confessio alibi, nec caetera hic. Enimvero non alibi caetera; itaque nec confessio in coelo. Aut si aliam volunt esse rationem interrogationis et confessionis coelestis, utique et ordinem suum illi struere debebunt alium longe, et ab ista dispositione diversum, quae Scripturis notatur, et possumus dicere, Viderint, dum hic ordo terrenae interrogationis et confessionis, ex materia decurrens persecutionis et discordiae publicae in nomen, salvus sit suae fidei; ut ita credendum sit sicut et scribitur, ita intelligendum sit sicuti auditur. Hic omnem ordinem sustineo, ipso Domino non aliam regionem mundi destinante. Quid enim post confessionis et negationis terminum subjungit? Ne putaveritis venisse me uti pacem mittam in terram; non veni, sed ut machaeram, certe in terram. Veni enim dividere hominem adversus patrem suum, et filiam adversus matrem suam, et socrum adversus nurum suam: et inimici homini domestici sui. Sic enim efficitur, ut tradat frater fratrem in mortem, et pater filium, et insurgant filii in parentes, et mori eos faciant. Et qui sustinuerit in finem, hic salvus erit. Adeo totus hic ordo dominicae machaerae, non in coelum missae, sed in terram, illic constituit etiam confessionem, quae in finem sustinendo passura est mortem.
pass_a_gloss: But those who think that the confession is not established here, that is, not within this circle of the earth, nor through this journey of life, nor among men of this common nature, what presumption is it against all order of things on this earth and in this life and under human powers to be experienced? For when souls have departed from bodies and have begun to be examined by command through the individual stories of the heavens and to be questioned about those secret sacraments of the heretics, then they will have to confess among the true powers and true men, namely Theletos and Abascantos and Acinetos of Valentinus. For our people, they say, not even the Demiurgus himself consistently approved men to be true, whom he assigned to be like the dripping of a pot and the dust of the earth and spittle and locusts; he also equated them with irrational beasts. It is written plainly. Nevertheless, this is not why another kind of man should be understood apart from us, whom it is agreed exist and who could have been used for comparison, while preserving both the property of the kind and singularity. For even if life is corrupted, so that it may be judged contemptible in comparison with the contemptible, nature is not immediately abolished, so that another nature may be assigned in its name. But nature is preserved, even if life is corrupted, and Christ does not know any other men than those about whom he says: 'Whom do men say that I am?' and 'How do you want men to do to you, and so you do to them.' See whether he has preserved the kind, from whom he also expects testimony of himself and in whom he commands the duty of justice. But if I were to ask to be shown those heavenly men, Aratus would more easily depict Perseus and Cepheus and Erigone and Ariadne among the stars. Who, however, prevented the Lord from determining there that a confession of men should also be made manifest, where he openly proclaimed his future, so that it would be established: 'Whoever has confessed me before men on earth, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven?' He ought to have rescued me from this error of earthly confession, which he did not want to receive, if he had commanded a heavenly one, because I knew no other men except the inhabitants of the earth; not even the man in heaven was yet seen by me. What faith is there in things, so that after passing away I may be lifted up to heavenly things and proved there, where I could not be imposed unless already proved? There I would be examined by command, where I could not arrive unless admitted. Heaven lies open to the Christian before the way, because there is no way to heaven except to one for whom heaven lies open; whoever has touched it will enter. What gatekeeper powers do you affirm for me, according to the Roman superstition, some Janus and Forculus and Limentinus? What powers do you arrange at the gates? If you have ever read in David, 'Remove your gates, princes, and the eternal gates will be lifted up, and the king of glory will enter,' and also if you have heard in Amos: 'Who builds his ascent to the heavens and founds his abundance on the earth; know that his ascent from there is made smooth by the footsteps of the Lord, and his entrance from there is opened by the powers of Christ,' and no delay or questioning will occur to Christians at the threshold, who will not be distinguished there but recognized, and not questioned but admitted. For even if you still think that heaven is closed, remember that the Lord left its keys here to Peter, and through him to the rest of the Church, which each one, having been questioned and confessed, will carry with him. But the devil asserts that confession must be made there, so that he may persuade negation here. I will certainly bring forth beautiful documents, I will carry good keys with me, the fear of those who can only kill the body but do nothing to the soul; I will be commended for the abandonment of this command; I will stand honorably in the heavenly places, who could not stand on earth; I will endure greater powers, who yielded to lesser ones; I will finally deserve to be admitted, now excluded. It is still possible to say: if confession is to be made in heaven, and negation here; for where one is, the other is also; rival things run together. Persecution must also be stirred up in heaven, which is the material for confession or negation. Why, then, do you hesitate, most audacious heretic, to transfer the entire order of Christian agitation to the heavenly places, and first of all to establish the hatred of the name there, where Christ presides at the right hand of the Father? You will establish there the synagogues of the Jews, the sources of persecutions, among whom the apostles suffered lashes, and the peoples of the nations with their own circus, where they easily cry out, 'How long until the third kind?' But you ought to exhibit our brothers and fathers and sons and mothers-in-law and daughters-in-law and our household members there, through whom the tradition is arranged; also kings and presidents and armed powers, among whom the case is to be purified. There will certainly be a prison in heaven, lacking the sun, or shining with unpleasant light, and chains perhaps made of straps, and a rack which is the axis itself that twists; then if a Christian is to be stoned, hailstones will be at hand; if he is to be burned, lightning will be before him; if he is to be killed, the armed hands of Orion will work; if he is to be finished by beasts, the seven stars of the north will send out bears, and the zodiac will send out bulls and lions. Whoever endures these things to the end will be saved. Is the end, then, and passion, and killing, and first confession in heaven? And where is the flesh, necessary for all these things? Where is the body, which alone can be killed by men? This certain reason has commanded us, and no one will push away the objection of this prescription, so that we are not forced to transfer the entire order of persecution, the entire firm preparation of its cause, to the place where he has given a forum for confession. For if confession is derived from persecution, and persecution ends in confession, they cannot but follow one another, since they arrange both the beginning and the end, that is, the entrance and exit. Furthermore, the hatred of the name will be here, and persecution will break out here, and tradition will produce here, and questioning will compel here, and carnage will rage here, and the entire order of confession or negation will be destroyed on earth. Therefore, if the other things are here, confession is not elsewhere; if confession is elsewhere, the other things are not here. For the other things are not elsewhere; therefore, confession is not in heaven. But if they want to be another reason for heavenly questioning and confession, they will certainly have to construct another order for it, far different from this arrangement, which is noted in the Scriptures, and we can say, 'Let them see to it,' as long as this order of earthly questioning and confession, proceeding from the material of persecution and public discord against the name, is preserved in its faith; so that it may be believed as it is written, and understood as it is heard. I sustain the entire order here, with the Lord himself not designating another region of the world. For what does he add after the end of confession and negation? 'Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth; I have not come to bring peace, but a sword, certainly on earth.' For I have come to divide a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law; and a man's enemies will be those of his own household. For thus it happens that a brother hands over a brother to death, and a father his son, and sons rise up against their parents and make them die. And whoever endures to the end will be saved. So the entire order of the Lord's sword is not sent to heaven but to earth, and it establishes confession there, which will suffer death by enduring to the end.

choices.why: The Latin phrase 'in terris' is more accurately translated as 'on earth' rather than 'in the world'.
The Latin phrase 'coelestes homines' refers to men in heaven, rather than a separate kind of man.
The Latin word 'machaeera' is a metaphor for division and conflict, rather than a literal sword.
The Latin phrase 'in finem' indicates a duration of time, rather than a spatial location.
The Latin phrase 'salvus erit' is in the future tense, indicating a future state of being saved.

bible_refs.note: The Lord says that whoever confesses him before men, he will also confess before his Father in heaven.
The Lord says that he has come to bring a sword, not peace, and that a man's enemies will be those of his own household.
The Psalmist says to remove the gates and let the king of glory enter.
The prophet Amos says that the Lord builds his ascent to the heavens and founds his abundance on the earth.

pass_b_english: But consider those who think the confession is not established here—not within this circle of earth, nor through this journey of life, nor among human beings of this common nature. What sheer presumption against the whole order of things on this earth, in this life, under human powers that must be experienced!
